verdict.rationale: React's docs say adding @types/react and @types/react-dom gives "full React Web support" in TypeScript, and that you can type component props. That typing is what an editor's TypeScript language service uses for completions and type errors, but the docs never describe the editor-side autocompletion or inline diagnostics themselves. The editor-setup page covers ESLint hooks rules, which is linting rather than a type language service, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of editor autocompletion and inline type-error diagnostics, a documented language service or editor plugin integration, and independent hands-on corroboration of accuracy.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get accurate autocompletion and inline type errors in my editor via a language service integration

citations.quote: you can get full React Web support by adding @types/react and @types/react-dom to your project.
The key difference when working with a component is that you can provide types for your component's props.
